Use these examples to move from a fitted model to comparisons, predictions,
custom formula transforms and inference. The [function reference](/reference/index.qmd)
gives the exact parameters; the [fitted-result overview](/reference-guide/fitted-results.qmd)
explains the objects returned by estimation.

## Fit and compare specifications

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pyfixest as pf

# Synthetic data include regressors, instruments and fixed-effect identifiers.
data = pf.get_data(seed=1234)
fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1 + f2", data=data, vcov={"CRV1": "f1"})
fit.tidy()
```

`fit.coef()`, `fit.se()`, `fit.tstat()` and `fit.pvalue()` extract individual
columns. `fit.confint()` returns confidence intervals. Tables can compare
several separately fitted results or a `FixestMulti` result:

```{python}
fits = pf.feols("Y ~ sw(X1, X2) | f1 + f2", data=data)
pf.etable(fits)
```

Use `fits.to_list()` for all individual results or `fits.fetch_model(0)` for
one. See [formula syntax](/tutorials/formula-syntax.qmd) for cumulative stepwise
models, multiple outcomes, sample splitting and interactions.

## Supply a custom formula transform

Pass functions explicitly through `context`, or use `context=0` to capture
names visible where you call the estimator. This continuous linear spline
has a knot at zero and separate slopes on either side:

```{python}
def linear_spline(x):
    return np.column_stack([np.minimum(x, 0), np.maximum(x, 0)])


spline_fit = pf.feols(
    "Y ~ linear_spline(X2) | f1 + f2",
    data=data,
    context={"linear_spline": linear_spline},
)
spline_fit.coef()
```

Compare it with explicitly created columns:

```{python}
spline_data = data.assign(X2_below=np.minimum(data["X2"], 0), X2_above=np.maximum(data["X2"], 0))
explicit_fit = pf.feols("Y ~ X2_below + X2_above | f1 + f2", data=spline_data)
pf.etable([spline_fit, explicit_fit])
```

## Fit an instrumental-variables model

Put endogenous variables and instruments inside `[endogenous ~ instruments]`.
An IV/2SLS call returns a `Feiv` result. Compute first-stage diagnostics and
inspect the first-stage regression through public state:

```{python}
fit_iv = pf.feols("Y ~ X2 + [X1 ~ Z1] | f1 + f2", data=data)
fit_iv.IV_Diag()
fit_iv.first_stage.diagnostics
```

```{python}
pf.etable([fit_iv.first_stage.model, fit_iv])
```

See the [IV result reference](/reference/estimation.models.feiv_.Feiv.qmd) for
supported diagnostics. Prediction and fixed-effect recovery are unavailable
for IV fits; the [support table](/reference-guide/model-support.qmd) lists
other estimator restrictions.

## Predict and recover fixed effects

```{python}
fit.predict()[:5]
fit.predict(newdata=data.head())
```

In-sample predictions follow the retained estimation sample. New-data
predictions follow the supplied rows, returning `NaN` for missing covariate or
fixed-effect inputs and unseen categorical/fixed-effect levels. Poisson offset
expressions that evaluate to missing values in `newdata` raise `ValueError`.
For GLMs, request `type="response"` for outcome-scale predictions; the default
is the link scale.

Recover a tidy table of fixed-effect coefficients:

```{python}
fixed_effects = fit.fixef()
fixed_effects.head()
```

`fit.fixef()` also creates `fit.fixef_estimates`; its `sumFE` array is the
fixed-effect contribution for each estimation-sample row. Individual levels
depend on the normalization described in the
[fixed-effect reference](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.fixef.qmd).

## Change inference after fitting

`fit.vcov()` updates the fitted result in place and returns that same result.
The next coefficient table uses the new covariance estimate:

```{python}
fit.vcov("hetero").tidy()
```

For simultaneous intervals on selected coefficients, use `inference_type="simult"`:

```{python}
fit.confint(keep=["X1", "X2"], exact_match=True, inference_type="simult", reps=999, seed=123)
```

See [wild bootstrap](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.wildboottest.qmd),
[randomization inference](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.ritest.qmd),
[multiple testing](/reference/estimation.post_estimation.multcomp.rwolf.qmd)
and [sequential inference](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.evalue.qmd)
for methods with additional sampling and model requirements. Choose the
covariance at estimation time when using `lean=True`; the
[storage guide](/reference-guide/model-storage.qmd) explains which operations
need retained data.

## Decompose a coefficient difference

The Gelbach decomposition explains the change between a short-regression
coefficient and the coefficient after adding covariates. This example computes
point estimates; leave `only_coef=False` to include bootstrap inference.

```{python}
from pyfixest.utils.dgps import gelbach_data

mediation_data = gelbach_data(nobs=500)
mediation_fit = pf.feols("y ~ x1 + x21 + x22 + x23", data=mediation_data)
decomposition = mediation_fit.decompose(decomp_var="x1", only_coef=True)
decomposition.tidy(panels="levels")
```

See [decompose()](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.decompose.qmd) for
grouping covariates, clustering and the returned object's tables and plots.
